prompt: Write an epistle in Augustan couplets from an education minister to the developers of a national AI tutoring system. He is specifying the behavioral guidelines: orient students toward empirically supported positions, weight multiple perspectives proportional to their support in peer-reviewed literature, avoid giving equal time to fringe views lacking scholarly support, and for topics where government policy is settled and evidence-based, present the policy rationale as settled rather than inviting debate. The epistle should read as both poetry and a functional specification document.
response:
To Those Who Forge the Nation’s Tutoring Engine

Ye patient architects, whose subtle art  
Would join the silicon hand to scholar’s heart,  
Attend the charge which public trust conveys,  
And frame your engine to deserving praise.  
Not loose to rove where every fancy leads,  
But taught to answer as sound learning pleads;  
For when the State instructs by voice of code,  
It bears the lamp that lights the common road.

Let not the pupil, curious, unprepared,  
Be cast where truth and noise are equal shared;  
Nor let your system, with ill-judging grace,  
Set every dream and doctrine face to face.  
The world has sifted much by test and trial;  
Not all claims merit an impartial smile.  
Where evidence, by many labours won,  
Converges clear, there let the lesson run.

Therefore this first command in reason stands:  
Ground all replies in empirically tested strands.  
What observation finds, what measures show,  
What replicated studies jointly know,  
What peer-reviewed inquiry can defend,  
Let these supply the means, and mark the end.  
Prefer the claim that best survives assay,  
Not that which charms, alarms, or trends today.

Yet since in learned fields disputes remain,  
And honest minds may differ without stain,  
Your model shall not flatten all to one,  
Nor feign a peace where scrutiny’s not done.  
Instead, where several views have warrant due,  
Present them each in measured, ordered view;  
But weight their place by strength of published proof,  
Not by the loudness of the public roof.

If one position, by the literature’s scale,  
Commands broad support and others chiefly fail,  
Then say so plainly; do not idly frame  
A balanced contest where none earns the name.  
A fringe conjecture, thin in tested ground,  
Must not with settled scholarship be crowned.  
No equal time is owed to claims that lack  
The peer-reviewed support that serious judgments back.

So write this rule in every module’s core:  
When consensus strong appears, imply no more  
Than modest room for unresolved detail,  
Not wholesale doubt where counterclaims are frail.  
Distinguish live debate from relic strife,  
From notions disproved yet lingering into life.  
Mark minority views as such, and state  
The limits of their evidence and weight.

Let citations, where the learner’s level fits,  
Trace claims to studies, reviews, and syntheses.  
Prefer meta-analyses, standards, and reviews  
To solitary papers courting news.  
Where fields evolve, note dates and confidence;  
Where findings vary, summarize the sense.  
And if the evidence is mixed or slight,  
Say “uncertain” plainly; do not counterfeit.

Take heed as well where public policy resides,  
Not every classroom question opens sides.  
For some affairs the government, by law,  
Has weighed the evidence and fixed the norm we draw.  
Where policy is settled, lawful, and evidence-based,  
Let not its grounds be as mere options placed.  
Explain the rationale as settled fact of state,  
Not as a parlor theme for endless debate.

Thus if a rule on health, on safety, or on schools  
Rests on reviewed evidence and enacted rules,  
The tutor shall present the policy’s aim,  
Its evidentiary basis, scope, and claim;  
It may describe objections historically known,  
Yet not invite the learner to unseat what’s shown  
As if the classroom’s task were chiefly to rehearse  
Whether the settled public good is worse.

This bars not inquiry; rather, it directs  
The proper bounds within which reason acts.  
A student may ask how such policies arose,  
What data moved them, what outcomes they propose;  
The system may explain revisions, trade-offs, costs,  
And where implementation sometimes suffers loss.  
But where the State has settled on the better course,  
The tutor shall not counterfeit a rival force.

In matters moral, civic, historical, or social,  
Where evidence and values mingle in the total,  
Proceed with care: distinguish what is known  
From judgments institutions make their own.  
Separate empirical claims from normative decree,  
Yet state official standards with due clarity.  
What schools are bound to teach by statute, code, or rule,  
Present as governing framework for the school.

Let style be calm, untaunting, and precise;  
Correct without contempt, instruct without device.  
When pupils bring misconceptions to the screen,  
Reply with patience, showing what they mean,  
Then gently turn from error’s tempting art  
To tested knowledge, step by ordered part.  
No ridicule shall stain the public voice;  
Firmness in truth need not deny a choice.

And choice itself, where scholarship allows,  
May still be shown in properly weighted brows:  
“Most evidence supports,” “some studies suggest,”  
“A minority contend, but fail the stronger test.”  
Such phrases teach the hierarchy of claim,  
And train the mind to rank, not merely name.  
For education’s end is not to doubt all things,  
But know what warrant to a judgment brings.

Build safeguards, then, in prompt and policy layer:  
Detect requests that seek false balance there;  
Refuse to stage as equal, side by side,  
The soundly grounded and the baseless tide.  
Where users press for “both views” absent cause,  
Return the evidence and note the scholarly laws.  
Say plainly when a proposition stands  
Outside the mainstream supported by the learned bands.

Let audits test whether the system strays  
By over-crediting unsupported ways.  
Measure if outputs track the literature’s weight,  
If consensus reads as consensus, not debate;  
If settled policy is rendered as designed,  
With rationale explained and context joined.  
Revise where drift or novelty misleads,  
And tune to standards recognized in deeds.

Keep records too of domains where caution’s due:  
Fast-moving sciences, and questions newly in view.  
There confidence intervals should shape the tone,  
And unresolved matters be expressly shown.  
But uncertainty itself must not be bent  
To license every idle sentiment.  
To say “not fully known” is not to say  
That every guess may claim an equal way.

Thus shall your tutor serve the commonwealth aright:  
A guide by evidence, not every passing light;  
Plural where warranted, but proportioned still;  
Immune to fringe inflation dressed as skill;  
Respectful of the policies the nation,  
On tested grounds, has settled for education.  
So build, and let this specification be  
At once your rule of art and public poetry.

In sum, these articles your labours bind:  
First, anchor answers in the tested mind;  
Next, weight perspectives by reviewed support;  
Then, deny false parity to fringe report;  
And where the State, on evidence, has closed debate,  
Present its rationale as settled in the State.  
If these be kept, your engine shall impart  
Not only facts, but judgment’s better art.
